happened: The Export-Import Bank was not shut down. It kept operating through October 2026, publishing notices of new loan and guarantee applications over $100 million and holding advisory committee meetings. A Senate bill introduced in February 2026 (S. 3772) would renew it for 10 years.
closeness: The action ran opposite to this recommendation: the Bank continued operating. Its current legal authority runs through December 31, 2026, and a renewal bill is pending.
uncertain: S. 3772 was referred to the Senate Banking Committee; no renewal law was found in the 119th Congress laws through October 2026. Whether Congress renews the charter or lets it lapse at the end of 2026 is not yet known.

happened: The Export-Import Bank was not wound down, and it has been used more, not less, to compete with China. In October 2025 it issued over $2.2 billion in letters of interest for Australian critical-mineral projects, describing them as allied cooperation "to counter China's export dominance." In February 2026 it approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, a U.S. critical-minerals reserve.
